title: Common Pronunciation Practice
description: Practise commonly confused English sounds and word endings with simple examples and a daily pronunciation routine.
learning_objectives: Build a short daily speaking routine

body_markdown:
## 1. Clear speech is more important than speed

Good pronunciation helps people understand you. You do not need to copy a particular accent. Aim for clear sounds, steady pace and complete word endings.

## 2. Practise these sound pairs

Read each pair slowly. Notice how the mouth and tongue move.

| Sound focus | Words to practise |
|---|---|
| V and W | vine / wine, vest / west |
| S and SH | sip / ship, see / she |
| Short I and long EE | sit / seat, ship / sheep |
| T and TH | tin / thin, tree / three |

Do not rush. Listen to a reliable dictionary audio pronunciation and repeat each word.

## 3. Practise final sounds

Say the final sound clearly:

- work
- help
- desk
- want
- asked
- worked

Do not add an extra vowel after the final consonant. For example, practise “work” as one syllable.

## 4. Practise plural and past endings

The ending **-s** can sound like /s/ in “books” or /z/ in “bags”. The ending **-ed** can sound different in “worked”, “played” and “wanted”.

Repeat:
- books, bags, watches
- worked, played, wanted

## 5. Daily five-minute routine

1. Listen to five words.
2. Repeat each word slowly.
3. Say each word in a sentence.
4. Record your voice.
5. Listen again and notice which sound needs more practice.

## 6. Practice sentences

- We will visit the west side.
- She can see three green trees.
- I worked at the desk yesterday.
- He wants to help us.

Read each sentence twice: first slowly, then at a natural pace.

## 7. Self-check

Can a listener understand every word? Are you saying the last sound? Are you speaking too quickly? Repeat the sentence if needed.

faq.question: Do I need a British or American accent?
faq.answer: No. Focus on clear, understandable pronunciation rather than copying a particular accent.

faq.question: How can I improve difficult sounds?
faq.answer: Listen to a reliable audio example, repeat slowly and practise the sound in short words and sentences.

faq.question: How long should I practise pronunciation daily?
faq.answer: Five to ten focused minutes every day is a useful starting routine.
